note: Two apparent warning signs in this year turn out not to be a change of president. The Herald headline of 10 January 1991, 'Michael Colvin fails on finals examinations', is an editorial attacking his proposal for comprehensive final exams, not a report of academic failure; the same issue quotes him as sitting ASG president. The two officers who stepped down on 17 January 1991 were judicial council chairman Amos Gott, who took a part-time university staff job that made him ineligible, and public relations vice president Van Hodge, who cited workload. Colvin was still presiding on 9 April 1991. This corrects the 1990-91 organization block in years.json, which lists Gott's and Hodge's offices as unknown.

note: Coates and 'Amanda Lich' are not two office-holders. Coates won the presidency in a recount on 15 April 1999, was covered as president through the autumn, and gave the Herald a year-end reflection as president on 25 April 2000. No 1999-2000 source found uses the surname Lich, which appears only on the Chambers plaque. The 27 April 1999 headline 'Ryan Morrison Wins Student Government Association Election' is not a presidential result: the Judicial Council voided the vice president of finance race over Joe Matheis's election code violations, and Morrison beat Matheis 346-99 in the re-run on 26 April 1999. That means the years.json organization block for 1999-00, which lists Matheis as vice president of finance, records the overturned result rather than the final one.
